title: Adaptive tiered-KV allocator with pipeline-cooperative mapping for multi-GPU memory
creator: Avery Chen
description: Problem: As models and request patterns grow, KV cache memory on multi-GPU nodes exhibits inefficient utilization under mixed tensor/pipeline parallel topologies. Small hot-key partitions lead to fragmentation and imbalanced memory pressure across devices, causing unnecessary KV spill, cross-GPU traffic, and throughput regressions. Goal: implement an allocator that reduces fragmentation, honors pipeline/tensor parallel boundaries, and supports low-latency continuous batching without increasing synchronization costs.
proposed_solution: Introduce a two-tier KV allocator: a hot-tier (fine-grained micro-slices) and a cold-tier (coarse slabs). Hot-tier is mapped greedily on-device with strict affinity; cold-tier uses cross-GPU pooled slabs that can be remapped during low-load windows.

Coordinator running on the runtime control plane maintains per-actor heuristics: key access frequency, sequence-length distribution, and pipeline-stage affinity. Coordinator suggests placement hints; local device allocator enforces hard affinity only for hot-tier objects to avoid runtime stalls.

Placement algorithm integrates tensor-parallel group topology: prefer colocating KV slices with the compute owner for that tensor shard. For pipeline parallelism, ensure sequential pipeline stages minimize cross-GPU KV hops by aligning cache locks to stage ownership where possible.

Eviction policy: hybrid LRU-DRAM + time-windowed read-frequency. Cold-tier can be asynchronously compacted and migrated via RDMA or NVLink transfers during controlled background windows to avoid tail-latency spikes.

Provide a fast-path for inference-serving threads: thread-local prefetch buffer of hot keys, populated by lightweight sampling and maintained lock-free using epoch counters to reduce contention under continuous batching.
Expose config knobs to Console: hot-tier size ratio, migration window duration, per-model affinity enforcement, and spill thresholds for Dedicated vs Hosted tiers.
Fallback behavior: if a device is overloaded, coordinator can fallback to model-quantized cold-tier variants to reduce memory footprint and keep SLOs.
Backward compatibility: support existing KV serialization and the current multi-GPU spill protocol, adding a negotiation step in session setup to advertise tier-aware capabilities.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration test that runs a 8-node pipeline+tensor-parallel model with simulated mixed-length traffic and demonstrates >=20% reduction in cross-GPU KV transfers compared to baseline
95th percentile tail latency does not regress more than 5ms under our continuous-batching harness for the target model family
Memory fragmentation metric (free contiguous bytes/total) improves by >=25% on average across nodes
Console exposes hot/cold tier metrics and the changeset includes at least two guardrail config toggles
Graceful fallback path verified: when hot-tier is disabled via config, system behaves identically to current baseline

technical_notes: Memory accounting: maintain per-GPU free lists for hot-tier micro-slices and a coarse slab allocator for cold-tier. Use 64B micro-slice granularity to reduce internal fragmentation for hot keys.

Locking: hot-tier operations should be single-atomic compare-and-swap updates to epoch counters to avoid per-key locks. Cold-tier compaction uses epoch quiescence and a background thread per NUMA domain.
Network/migration: leverage NVLink for intra-node transfers and RDMA/NVMe for inter-node cold migration. Use delta-encoded serialization for KV entries to reduce transfer size.

Pipeline integration: add a placement hint to each pipeline checkpoint so that the runtime can prefer local cache reads for adjacent stages; include a small metadata header in KV entries with owner-stage id.
Prefetch heuristic: sample the last N requests per route to build a tiny bloom filter of hot keys; use this for thread-local prefetch buffers updated every 50ms.
Telemetry: track per-key hit rate, migration count, transfer bytes, and lock contention events. Add derived metric: cross_gpu_kv_transfer_per_token.

Tradeoffs: stricter affinity reduces cross-GPU traffic but can cause uneven memory pressure; background migration amortizes imbalance but must be throttled to avoid latency spikes. We choose conservative default knobs and expose tuning parameters.
Compatibility: session-capability-negotiation allows older clients to continue without tiered placement. Coordinator maintains a compatibility map for mixed clusters.
testing_plan: Unit tests for allocator invariants: no double-free, correct accounting under concurrent alloc/free
Microbenchmarks: allocate/free latency for hot-tier and cold-tier; compare to baseline allocators
Integration tests: 4x GPU and 8x GPU topologies with tensor/pipeline mixes and stochastic sequence lengths
Chaos testing: kill a device during background migration and verify no corruption and correct fallback
Performance regression suite: measure cross-GPU bandwidth and token throughput under our continuous-batching harness
rollout_and_monitoring: Start with canary on a Dedicated pool limited to non-critical traffic and monitor cross_gpu_kv_transfer_per_token and tail latency
Gate with a dashboard alert if migration throughput exceeds 200 MB/s per node or tail latency exceeds baseline +5ms
Provide a one-click kill switch per pool to disable tiered allocation and revert to baseline during incidents
Post-mortem runbook: steps to drain migrations, disable prefetchers, and force serialize cold-tier before rolling nodes back
comments: 2026-02-18: Initial design doc posted to Confluence and shared with serving-runtime and infra teams. Feedback: prefer NVLink first for intra-node moves (A. Singh).
2026-02-25: Architecture review with Research. Decided on two-tier approach instead of full dynamic rebalance due to risk of tail-latency during migration (notes linked).
2026-03-02: Prototype for hot-tier allocator implemented. Microbenchmarks show 40% lower per-key alloc latency vs baseline under contention. Raised PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1248
2026-03-08: Design feedback from Natalia (SRE): add throttling control for background migration; updated proposed solution accordingly.
2026-03-10: Began integration test harness for pipeline-aware placement. Noted a regression in a 2-stage pipeline where owner-stage metadata was not propagated; tracking under ENG-70812.
